verdict.rationale: Gmail's own marketing says Gemini helps draft and polish emails and that suggested replies let you 'reply in one click, in your voice', and the help docs describe drafting and refining for tone. The voice claim is only a one-line marketing statement. Hands-on users report that the related 'improve' feature can strip personal voice or turn a warm email cold, which casts doubt on how well tone is matched, though it does not directly test suggested replies. Missing for 10: documentation of how personal voice and style are learned or applied, evidence that full reply drafts (not just one-click suggestions) match the user's tone, and independent corroboration that output avoids generic boilerplate.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, AI drafts replies in my own voice and tone — ready to review and send, not generic boilerplate

citations.quote: Gemini in Gmail saves you time drafting or polishing emails, and suggested replies help you reply in one click, in your voice.
Draft: Create new emails or refine existing drafts for tone and clarity.
